runtime_expectations.reason: This group is the first to add a frontend surface (E2-S3 stands up the entire Vite/React/TS scaffold). Backend-only AC coverage (E3-S3, E4-S2, E6-S4, E7-S3, E8-S2, E10-S2) is treated the same as Groups C/D: pytest's api/unit suites exercise the real `src.app.main.app` object through FastAPI's TestClient, which is judged live-equivalent and does not require a separately started uvicorn process to also be probed with curl. E2-S3's playwright_checks are different in kind: role-based redirect after login is an integration behavior spanning the real SPA (built and served, or `npm run dev`) talking to the real backend API (`uv run uvicorn src.app.main:app`) with a real JWT round-trip — vitest component tests (Login.test.tsx, AuthContext.test.tsx) cannot substitute for this because the redirect decision depends on the router wiring in App.tsx/router.tsx, which is not itself unit-testable in isolation. The evaluator MUST start both processes for the playwright_checks section; the api_checks and unit_test_checks sections may be satisfied by the pytest suite alone.

E3-S3 AC2. Same for advisor- and admin-role tokens against the same path.
E3-S3 AC3. No write verb is registered on /api/audit; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE all return 405, not 404 or 403 — the route exists, the method does not.
E3-S3 AC4. Every returned entry has entity_type == 'RiskBandAssignment' exactly, none of the other 8 entity types leak in.
E6-S4 AC1; api-contracts.md §8.1. Current holdings and drift per asset class.
E6-S4 AC2; api-contracts.md §12.1. First call for a new simulated day succeeds and returns the response shape shared with E7-S3/E8-S2's counts.
E6-S4 AC3. Same for an advisor-role token.
E6-S4 AC4. Second immediate call for the same simulated day maps ConflictError(DAY_ALREADY_ADVANCED) to 409; no duplicate NavSnapshot rows are created either way.
E6-S4 AC5. Empty holdings is a 200 with an empty list, not an error.

still on an authenticated route, not redirected back to /login

design_checks.notes: Login is the only UI surface this group ships (Dashboard/Questionnaire/etc. land in later groups and only need a stub route for the redirect target to resolve). At 1280px: centered single-column form, no dead whitespace sprawl. At 375px: form remains single-column, no horizontal scroll, tap targets (email/password/submit) at least 40px tall. accessibility carries the highest bar (7) because E2-S3 AC3 is an explicit, testable acceptance criterion (for/id label association), not just a design nicety — visible :focus outline on inputs and the submit button is part of that bar. The design-critic should score against the mockup's aesthetic direction, not against the mockup's literal markup — production code is not expected to reuse the mockup's inline <style> block verbatim.

typing.command: cd backend && uv run mypy src/
typing.description: mypy exits 0 across src/ including this group's 6 new backend modules and 2 extended router-registration points in app/main.py.

frontend_typing.description: First frontend TypeScript check in the pipeline. tsc --noEmit (or the project's equivalent script) exits 0 with zero `any` per CLAUDE.md's static-typing rule; entities.ts from E1-S1 (Group A) is the only pre-existing frontend type source this group's new files may import from.

frontend_lint.description: ESLint clean on all new frontend/src files, using the eslint.config.js this story itself creates.

traces: system-design.md D3 ('Routers may not import repositories')
layering.command: rg -n "^\s*(from|import)\s+(src\.)?app\b" backend/src/domain backend/src/db ; rg -n "^\s*(from|import)\s+(src\.)?domain\.[a-z_]+\.(repository|threshold_repository)\b" backend/src/app ; rg -n "^\s*(from|import)\s+(src\.)?db\.models\b" backend/src/app ; rg -n "raise HTTPException" backend/src/domain
layering.description: Same four static scans carried forward unchanged. This group's two new routers (audit.py, holdings.py) and the extended admin.py must call domain/*/service.py functions only, never a repository or db.models directly, and must never raise HTTPException from inside src/domain.

no_float.description: Extends the existing scan to this group's three new pure-computation modules: domain/risk_profile/scoring.py (point totals and band-threshold comparisons), domain/goals/progress.py (percent_complete = current_value * 10000 / target_amount, capped at 20000 bps), and domain/rebalancing/engine.py (BUY/SELL amount and unit proposals). No float literal, float() call, or -> float annotation may appear in any of the three, or in domain/admin/service.py.

audit_writer_single_call.command: cd backend && uv run pytest tests/unit/test_risk_profile_service.py tests/unit/test_rebalancing_service.py tests/unit/test_admin_publish_service.py
audit_writer_single_call.description: Each of the three new/extended services (risk_profile scoring, rebalancing evaluation, admin publish) calls domain.audit.service.write_audit_entry exactly once per successful write, verified via a spy/mock asserting assert_called_once() with the correct entity_type (RiskBandAssignment, RebalancingRecommendation, and RiskBandRule/AllocationTemplate/RebalancingThreshold respectively).

goal_progress_idempotent.command: cd backend && uv run pytest tests/unit/test_goal_progress.py
goal_progress_idempotent.description: Idempotency for a given price_date relies on the UNIQUE(goal_id, price_date) constraint on GoalProgressSnapshot (already migrated in Group C), not a check-then-act read; a second recompute call for the same price_date must not create a second row for the same goal.

kyc_gate.command: cd backend && uv run pytest tests/unit/test_rebalancing_service.py -k kyc
kyc_gate.description: A customer with kyc_verified = false produces no RebalancingRecommendation even when drift exceeds threshold — the one real gating branch for the Customer.kyc_verified stub flag.

template_sum_and_questionnaire_length.command: cd backend && uv run pytest tests/unit/test_admin_publish_service.py
template_sum_and_questionnaire_length.description: domain/admin/service.py rejects (a) an AllocationTemplate whose percent_bps do not sum to exactly 10000 and (b) a RiskBandRule with fewer than 6 questions, in both cases before any row reaches the repository — this is the service-layer gate in front of E10-S1's repository-layer/architecture-test enforcement of the same rule, not a duplicate no-op.

publish_version_race.command: cd backend && uv run pytest tests/unit/test_admin_publish_service.py -k conflict
publish_version_race.description: Two concurrent publish calls for the same next version are serialized so exactly one succeeds; the loser's IntegrityError (from E10-S1's UNIQUE(version) / UNIQUE(risk_band, version) constraints) is translated to ConflictError, mapped to 409 at the router layer (already-registered VERSION_CONFLICT mapping from Group D's error_handlers.py).

migrations_unchanged.command: git diff --stat <last-group-D-tip-commit>..HEAD -- backend/alembic/versions/ backend/alembic.ini backend/alembic/env.py backend/alembic/script.py.mako
migrations_unchanged.description: Must produce empty output. This group adds no new table and needs no schema change — every entity these 7 stories touch (RiskBandRule, RiskBandAssignment, Holding, NavSnapshot, Goal, GoalProgressSnapshot, RebalancingRecommendation, RebalancingThreshold, AuditLogEntry) was already migrated by Group B/C's revision chain.

env_vars.command: cd backend && uv run detect-secrets scan src seed && cd ../frontend && npx detect-secrets scan src
env_vars.description: No new, unallowlisted finding. Extended to frontend/src this group since E2-S3 is the first story to write client-side token-handling code (frontend/src/api/client.ts, frontend/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx); the JWT itself is runtime data, not a hardcoded secret, so it must not trip this scan.

unit_test_checks.assertion: roleRedirect(role) returns the correct landing path for each of customer/advisor/admin/compliance; Login.tsx calls navigate() with that path immediately after a successful login response.
Submitting the form with a mocked 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS response renders an inline error message and does not call navigate().
The rendered DOM has label[for=email]/input#email and label[for=password]/input#password pairs (queried via getByLabelText, not getByTestId).

After a successful login, the token is persisted (localStorage or equivalent) and api/client.ts's request wrapper attaches Authorization: Bearer <token> to a subsequent call, verified by inspecting the mocked fetch/axios call's headers.

Re-initializing AuthContext with a token already present in storage restores the authenticated session (calls GET /api/auth/me) without redirecting to /login, so a page refresh mid-session does not force re-login.

GET /api/audit with a compliance token and actor_id/entity_type/from/to query params returns 200 with a body matching AuditPage's total/limit/offset/entries shape, entries filtered to the given params.
GET /api/audit with a customer-, advisor-, or admin-role token each return 403 ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED (parametrized over the three roles).
POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE to /api/audit each return 405 (FastAPI's own method-not-allowed on a route with only GET registered), not 404 or 403.

GET /api/audit?entity_type=RiskBandAssignment against a seeded/audited fixture containing multiple entity_types returns only RiskBandAssignment rows; the other 8 entity_type values in AuditLogEntry's CHECK set are all present in the fixture and all excluded from this response.
GET /api/audit with no Authorization header returns 401 TOKEN_MISSING.
score_answers(answers, rule) called twice with the identical answers dict returns the identical risk_band string both times.
Submitting fewer answers than the active questionnaire's question count raises ValidationError (INCOMPLETE_QUESTIONNAIRE); no RiskBandAssignment or RiskProfileAnswer row is persisted.
A successful submit_risk_profile call inserts one RiskBandAssignment row with customer_id, risk_band, rule_version, and assigned_at all correctly populated, readable back via the repository.
A successful call invokes the audit-writer exactly once with entity_type='RiskBandAssignment' (MagicMock spy, assert_called_once()).
No float type appears anywhere in score_answers's point totals, thresholds, or return value; type() introspection confirms int/Decimal only.
Submitting a full answer set twice for the same customer inserts two distinct RiskBandAssignment rows (distinct ids, both queryable); the first row's fields are unchanged after the second submit.

GET /api/holdings for a customer with seeded holdings returns 200 with holdings[] entries each containing current_value, current_percent, target_percent, drift_percent, exceeds_threshold matching drift.py's computation.
POST /api/admin/advance-day with an admin token returns 200 with price_date equal to the day after the previously latest NavSnapshot date.
POST /api/admin/advance-day with a customer-role token and, separately, an advisor-role token, both return 403 ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED.

Two POST /api/admin/advance-day calls in immediate succession: first returns 200, second returns 409 DAY_ALREADY_ADVANCED; the NavSnapshot table has no duplicate (asset_class_id, price_date) rows after both calls.
GET /api/holdings for a customer with zero Holding rows returns 200 with holdings: [], total_value: '0.00', as_of_date: null — not a 404 or 500.
After one advance_day() call, every active Goal for a customer with holdings has exactly one new GoalProgressSnapshot, timestamped to the call's snapshot_at.

compute_percent_complete(current_value, target_amount) == round_half_up(current_value * 10000 / target_amount) bps, capped at 20000 (200.00%); a current_value far exceeding target_amount is capped, not left unbounded.
compute_percent_complete(0, target_amount) returns 0 without raising ZeroDivisionError or any other exception.
Calling the recompute step twice for the same price_date does not create a second GoalProgressSnapshot row for the same goal_id (relies on UNIQUE(goal_id, price_date)).
Calling holdings/service.py's advance_day() end-to-end asserts a new GoalProgressSnapshot exists for a seeded active goal immediately afterward, with no separate manual recompute call in the test.

A customer with at least one asset class's drift exceeding the active threshold gets one RebalancingRecommendation with proposed_actions_json containing BUY/SELL entries whose amounts move current_percent toward target_percent.
A customer whose drift is within threshold on every held asset class produces no RebalancingRecommendation row (no-op, not an empty-actions row).
A customer with zero Holding rows is a documented no-op — the service returns without raising and without inserting a recommendation.
A customer with kyc_verified = false and drift exceeding threshold on every asset class still produces no RebalancingRecommendation.
A successful recommendation-creating call invokes the audit-writer exactly once with entity_type='RebalancingRecommendation' (spy, assert_called_once()).
No float type appears in any proposed BUY/SELL amount, unit, or drift_percent value returned by engine.py; type() introspection confirms Decimal/int only.
publish_allocation_template with percent_bps summing to 9900 or 10100 raises ValidationError (TEMPLATE_SUM_INVALID) and no AllocationTemplate row is written.
publish_risk_band_rule with a questionnaire_json containing fewer than 6 questions raises ValidationError (QUESTIONNAIRE_TOO_SHORT) and no RiskBandRule row is written.
Two publish calls racing for the same risk_band's next version: the loser's repository-level IntegrityError is caught and re-raised as ConflictError; exactly one of the two calls succeeds.

Each of publish_risk_band_rule, publish_allocation_template, and publish_rebalancing_threshold invokes the audit-writer exactly once with entity_type matching the published entity (spy, assert_called_once()).
create_asset_class / update_asset_class with a code already used by another asset class raises a conflict (DUPLICATE_ASSET_CLASS_CODE) before any insert/update reaches the repository.

notes: 1. E2-S3 is the pivot point of the whole build: every later UI group (F/G/H) depends on the scaffold this story creates (main.tsx, router.tsx, AuthContext, api/client.ts, Layout/NavBar/LabeledField/ErrorMessage). The generator should treat file ownership here as strict and singular — no other Group E story touches frontend/ at all, so there is no cross-teammate contention on any frontend file this group.

2. Backend file contention within this group: backend/src/domain/holdings/service.py's advance_day() function is extended by BOTH E7-S3 (invoke goal-progress recompute) and E8-S2 (invoke rebalancing evaluation) — component-map.md lists both as 'Modifies' on the same file. The generator's dependency handshake for this group should sequence these two (or designate one as integrator) rather than spawning both against advance_day() in parallel, to avoid a merge conflict inside one function body. E6-S4's routers/admin.py only calls advance_day(); it does not need to touch holdings/service.py itself.

3. E3-S3 and E6-S4 both modify backend/src/app/main.py (new router registration) and backend/src/app/error_handlers.py (E6-S4 needs DAY_ALREADY_ADVANCED -> 409, already partially scaffolded in Group D's error_handlers.py per D.json's file list). Treat main.py as an integration point: each router's registration is a one-line addition, low collision risk, but should still land in a single commit per the file-ownership discipline.

4. playwright_checks pw-e-01 through pw-e-03 assume specific route paths (e.g. /customer/dashboard) inferred from story text and component-map.md file names (Dashboard.tsx, CustomerList.tsx, AdminHome.tsx, AuditLog.tsx), none of which are finalized until E2-S3's router.tsx is actually written. The evaluator should treat the exact path string as flexible and verify the *persona-to-screen mapping*, not a hardcoded URL, unless the generator's router.tsx fixes a specific convention worth pinning down in a follow-up contract revision.

5. Landing screens for customer/advisor/admin/compliance beyond Login itself (Dashboard, CustomerList, AdminHome, AuditLog) do not have their own stories in this group — E4-S4, E9-S4, E10-S4, E3-S4 build the real versions later. E2-S3's router.tsx therefore only needs a placeholder/stub route at each landing path sufficient to prove the redirect lands correctly; a fully-featured dashboard is out of scope for this group's contract and must not be scored as missing functionality here.

6. No new Alembic migration and no new append-only architecture-test case is required this group — every table these 7 stories touch was migrated in Group B/C, and E10-S2 is a service-layer story sitting entirely on top of E10-S1's already-tested (Group D) append-only repository guarantees.
